body:
WHAT
TEST tries the base URL exactly as typed, then (for `localhost`) the same URL with 127.0.0.1, then the stripped origin under each known OpenAI-compatible path: /v1, /v1/openai, /inference/v1, /openai/v1, /api/v1 — for any host. The first URL whose /models answers 200 (or whose chat route exists) is returned as `baseUrl`, and the wizard writes it back into the field so it is what gets saved.

WHY
Users paste the host from a provider's homepage or the URL their curl posts to; each provider hangs its API somewhere different, and the failure looked exactly like a bad key.

WHERE
app/main/connection.js — API_PATH_SUFFIXES, SUFFIXES_LONGEST_FIRST, stripApiSuffix(baseUrl), candidateBaseUrls(baseUrl), testEndpoint() loop returning { ok: true, baseUrl: candidate, models, contextLimit? }. app/main/config.js — normalizeBaseUrl() strips a pasted /chat/completions or /models first. app/renderer/modules/setup.js — TEST handler writes result.baseUrl into wizBaseUrlEl when it differs.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. candidateBaseUrls("http://localhost:1234") returns, in order, the URL as given, http://127.0.0.1:1234, then http://localhost:1234/v1, /v1/openai, /inference/v1, /openai/v1, /api/v1 with no duplicates and no trailing slashes.
2. candidateBaseUrls("https://api.example.com/v1/openai") strips the longest matching suffix first so candidates are built from https://api.example.com, never https://api.example.com/v1/openai/v1.
3. With a fake fetch that only answers 200 at https://host/openai/v1/models, testEndpoint on https://host returns ok:true and baseUrl "https://host/openai/v1" — the working candidate, not the typed one.
4. The as-given URL is fetched first; when it answers 200 no further candidate is requested (exactly one /models call).
5. A candidate whose fetch throws is skipped and the walk continues; if all throw, the last describeFetchError text is returned as error.
